thread:
maria: Heads-up, Acme is seeing a big spike in 429s and 3-5s tail latency on their dedicated endpoints since ~09:15 UTC. They're on Dedicated capacity (dedicated-acme-1).
kevin: Can you paste a sample request ID or tenant header?
maria: customer ticket includes request-id=rx-9f3b2 and header x-tenant: acme, x-tier: platinum. Happening across routes.
sam: I pulled metrics — spike aligns with a config rollout at 09:12 from controlplane (policy eval change).
irene: :eyes: which change? any CID or PR?
sam: PR 4892 rolled a policy change that added a new fallthrough rule to route evaluation. It touched cache keys for routeset evaluation.
maria: Acme reports some of their traffic got routed to shared pools and hit node-level rate limits. They say Dedicated pool still shows healthy available GPUs.
kevin: Oof. That sounds like a pool-selection flip. I grabbed router logs for the tenant. Snippet:```2026-03-16T09:15:06Z router INFO route_eval tenant=acme eval_id=ev-112 selected_pool=shared-cold-3 expected_pool=dedicated-acme-1 reason='cache-miss->fallback'```
alex: That 'cache-miss->fallback' wording matches a stale cache key path. The new policy changed the key structure so cached entries weren't matched and fell back to default routing.
eng-runtime: Confirmed. We see a burst of fallthrough decisions for the platinum tier between 09:12-09:22. Many requests hit shared pools and then throttled due to per-tenant burst caps on shared.
maria: Customer impact: ~8% request errors (429) for last 30m, several timeouts, billing churn concern. Customer on a committed reserved contract, so billing anomalies need support note.
kevin: Repro steps (dev): curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'x-tenant: acme' -H 'x-tier: platinum' 'https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate' -- you'll see 429s when routing goes to shared. If you add header 'x-force-pool: dedicated-acme-1' it bypasses policy and succeeds.
irene: Any quick mitigations for the customer while we fix controlplane?
sam: Short-term: 1) Pin the tenant to dedicated-acme-1 via per-tenant override (console toggle or api /admin/tenants/acme/override). 2) Temporarily increase dedicated-acme-1 burst quota. 3) Roll back the cache-key portion of PR 4892.
alex: I'll prepare the rollback PR and a hotfix to re-normalize cache keys.
eng-runtime: Also adding a probe to detect when expected_pool != selected_pool for >1% of requests in a minute and alert.
maria: I've created support case CS-78321 and notified Acme. Support-bot created ticket #CS-78321 and linked internal incident INC-2026-73.
support-bot: Ticket CS-78321 opened by maria. Priority: P1. Incident INC-2026-73 created and paged to eng-runtime oncall.
kevin: Quick root-cause hypothesis: policy eval cache schema changed -> existing cache entries became non-match -> evaluator fell back to default pool selection (shared) -> increased load on shared -> tenant hit shared pool rate cap -> 429s.
irene: Repro note for SRE: run this query on controlplane logs to enumerate affected tenants:```rg "selected_pool=.*fallback" /var/log/controlplane/*.log | cut -d' ' -f5- | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr```
alex: Action items: - alex: open rollback PR (in flight) - kevin: run tenant pin for acme + increase dedicated bursts - sam: watch telemetry and confirm error rate drops - irene: add alert and run postmortem template - maria: keep customer updated, include mitigation steps
kevin: Done: pinned tenant acme -> dedicated-acme-1 and bumped burst cap by 2x at 09:40. Early numbers show 429s down to <0.5% within 10m.
maria: Acme confirms errors subsided. They asked for a postmortem and billing credit eval for the degraded window.
eng-runtime: We'll ship rollback and cache-key normalization in a hotfix. Rolling to prod at 10:15 UTC unless objections.
sam: No objections. Please include canary in us-east-1 only first.
irene: I'll own the postmortem doc and link to CS-78321. Need timeline + logs + PR diffs.
maria: Thanks team. Tagging @kevin @alex for follow-ups with customer and eng notes. :heart:
kevin: Follow-up: created PR 4920 (rollback) and PR 4921 (cache-key hotfix). Monitoring for 24h.
alex: Logging improvement task: include expected_pool in router access logs to enable faster triage next time.
maria: Closing loop with Acme and drafting billing note. Will attach mitigation timeline and ask billing for credit eval.
eng-runtime: Incident INC-2026-73 will be updated with RCA once postmortem is done.
kevin: If anyone sees a similar spike, run quick check:```# check mismatch rate
curl 'https://controlplane.internal/admin/metrics?name=route_mismatch_rate' | jq .value
```
maria: Good runbook additions. Thanks all.
